subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw add YAML as a second supported core config-file format, or should the project keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` canonical and improve/document `openclaw config`/`config.patch` for comment-safe edits?
rationale: This changes the core config-file contract and upgrade surface, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces; automation cannot decide the product tradeoff from code alone.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Close or leave the feature unscheduled, and invest any follow-up in docs/prompts that steer users and agents to `openclaw config` and `config.patch`.

options.title: Approve YAML Support
options.body: Accept the new config surface only with explicit precedence rules, parser semantics, write-back behavior, reload behavior, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Programmatic Editing
options.body: Keep the file format unchanged while adding a narrower docs update about comment-aware edits and avoiding parse/dump round trips.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Close or leave the feature unscheduled, and invest any follow-up in docs/prompts that steer users and agents to `openclaw config` and `config.patch`.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across config CLI docs, config patch semantics, and current local blame for the config-file contract surface.
